question: True or false: a Cretan who says all Cretans always lie has produced a genuine paradox, true if false and false if true?
answer: False. If the sentence were true, the Cretan saying it would be lying, so it cannot be true. But it can simply be false: one Cretan who sometimes tells the truth suffices. The line is credited to the poet Epimenides; the New Testament letter to Titus quotes it and adds: this testimony is true.
move: The opposite of all is not none; it is merely not all.
ask: When I say 'everyone does it', do I mean everyone, or just not no one?
trap: Treating it as false means every Cretan always tells the truth.
reference: Prior, Epimenides the Cretan, Journal of Symbolic Logic 23 (3), 1958
